searchText: Does anyone have a link to an explanation of how exactly validators are shuffled into committees and how they propose and attest to shard states? I'm also trying to figure out exactly when validators are rewarded. Exactly once every epoch? Or is it probabilistic like in Tezos staking? <@575584687137882112> can explain more by your question of "how they propose and attest"? Do you mean the process of it? https://github.com/ethereum/eth2.0-specs/blob/dev/specs/core/0_beacon-chain.md#rewards-and-penalties-1 Rewards and penalties are calculated every epoch I'll look for an explainer, one sec https://notes.ethereum.org/jDcuUp3-T8CeFTv0YpAsHw?view#Epoch-Processing Scroll down to rewards and penalties, tad of explaining there My rough guess based on the AMA and other informal sources: 1. At each Epoch, every Validator is put into one slot in one random Committee, with every Committee being tied 1:1 to a Shard. 2. Each Committee have one proposer slot and x attester slots. 3. Every block the proposer proposes a block and the attesters attest to the block. 4. Repeat from step 1. Is that anywhere close to reality? Yes, every validator in a committee performs one action per epoch Only one proposer per slot per committee Ideally each committee should be TARGET_COMMITTEE_SIZE (128) or larger The proposer changes every slot Not only one slot per epoch There should be SLOTS_PER_EPOCH proposers in a committee every epoch Thanks, very useful info! So, we have enough attesters that several can attest to each block, but no one will attest more than once per Epoch? Exactly Are slots different than blocks or the same? **vbuterin** A slot is a period of time **vbuterin** A block appears in a particular slot Right, validators have the duration of the slot assigned to submit whats needed If they miss it they'll get penalized but the network would be fine A block not being submitted would delay justification right? If a block is missed, the assigned committee attests to their local head and just attests to a block at an earlier slot. There is also enough capacity in blocks (see constant `MAX_ATTESTATIONS`) such that enough attestations can be included in some subset of `SLOTS_PER_EPOCH` blocks to still justify something that epoch Got it, thanks 👍 Eth2 public call this thursday. Please add items to the agenda for discussion Agenda: https://github.com/ethereum/eth2.0-pm/issues/73

excerpts.author: svantetobias
excerpts.content:
My rough guess based on the AMA and other informal sources: 
1. At each Epoch, every Validator is put into one slot in one random Committee, with every Committee being tied 1:1 to a Shard. 
2. Each Committee have one proposer slot and x attester slots. 
3. Every block the proposer proposes a block and the attesters attest to the block.
4. Repeat from step 1.

Is that anywhere close to reality?

excerpts.author: kiwi.eth
excerpts.content: Yes, every validator in a committee performs one action per epoch

excerpts.author: kiwi.eth
excerpts.content: Only one proposer per slot per committee

excerpts.author: kiwi.eth
excerpts.content: Ideally each committee should be TARGET_COMMITTEE_SIZE (128) or larger

excerpts.author: kiwi.eth
excerpts.content: The proposer changes every slot

excerpts.author: kiwi.eth
excerpts.content: Not only one slot per epoch

excerpts.author: kiwi.eth
excerpts.content: There should be SLOTS_PER_EPOCH proposers in a committee every epoch

excerpts.author: svantetobias
excerpts.content: Thanks, very useful info! So, we have enough attesters that several can attest to each block, but no one will attest more than once per Epoch?
